checks.name: Period recovery
checks.detail: found the 14.1 ppt transit 3 more times in TESS (BTJD 1414.94, 1417.44, 1428.31; same depth and duration, above the 7.0σ false-alarm threshold); the dips don't fit one period without predicting a transit where TESS saw none: not one transiting body, or the repeats are something else; most probable P ≈ 108 d (68%: 98.3-139 d), from the periods the data allow, the transit probability and the shape's 1.45 d; a second transit fixes it: the next TESS sectors of the star, or ground photometry
checks.value: 16 sectors scanned (357 d): BTJD 1414.94, 20.2 ppt, SNR 11.6; BTJD 1417.44, 12.8 ppt, SNR 9.2; BTJD 1428.31, 13.2 ppt, SNR 23.9 · ZTF not used: the star (G 12.4) saturates it · 22% of 9.81-2000 d allowed by the TESS coverage

checks.name: Individual transits
checks.detail: one transit: the period is unknown
checks.value: BTJD 1426.30: vetting SNR 12.0, 11.9 ppt (the search's SNR was 32.2: a different detrending, binning and noise estimate)

checks.name: Event consistency
checks.detail: compares transits with each other: a periodic signal only

checks.name: Signal uniqueness (single event)
checks.detail: a brightening at BTJD 4017.39 is also above the false-alarm threshold: the systematics make events this size in both directions
checks.value: the dip 23.0σ white, 18.6σ red (F_red 1.24 from 3335 box positions over 354 d); threshold 4.5σ (noise reaches it anywhere in that much data 1% of the time); strongest brightening 10.7σ red at BTJD 4017.39

checks.name: SNR growth
checks.detail: how the SNR builds over transits: a periodic signal only

checks.name: Period consistency
checks.detail: one transit: there's no period to check (the alias and shape checks bound it instead)

checks.name: Alias periods
checks.detail: periods under 9.8 d would have shown a second transit in the data around the dip; on this star a 2.55 h transit needs P ≳ 0.8 d (central, circular orbit)

checks.name: Detrending sensitivity
checks.detail: survives 4 detrendings (two methods, transits masked) with the depth within 30%
checks.value: running median 0.5 d: 12.3 ppt (SNR 11.6); running median 1 d: 11.9 ppt (SNR 12.0); running median 2 d: 12 ppt (SNR 9.3); local quadratic 1.5 d: 10.9 ppt (SNR 6.1)

checks.name: Depth stability
checks.detail: one transit: nothing to compare its depth with (the pipeline and detrending checks test it instead)

checks.detail: one transit: there are no alternate transits to compare

checks.value: deepest other dip: BTJD 1428.32, 15.5 ppt (20.5σ red); limit for an eclipse anywhere in 354 d of data: 1.38 ppt (3σ red)

checks.name: Transit shape

checks.name: Duration vs expected

checks.name: Period from the transit shape
checks.detail: ingress not resolved (SNR 12.0, ingress 0.57 h)

checks.name: Variability at the transit period
checks.detail: no variability above 0.5 ppt out of transit (smaller pulsations are handled by the pulsation test)
checks.value: no significant variability in 8 sectors

checks.name: Pulsation removal
checks.detail: no significant pulsation or rotation signal to remove
checks.value: 0 periodic signals removed; transit 11.9 ppt (SNR 12.0) → 11.9 ppt (SNR 12.0), 8 sectors

checks.name: Archival radial velocities

checks.value: Gaia: 17 epochs, p(constant) 0.52, robust amplitude 15.6 km/s → K < 17.6 km/s

notes: Approximate re-implementation of TRICERATOPS (circular orbits, main-sequence companions, Sun-like hosts for background stars and for neighbours without a Gaia size); run TRICERATOPS/VESPA before claiming validation.
No high-resolution imaging: unresolved companions within ~1″ (74% of binaries at 489 pc) are allowed.
Archival RVs (K < 17.550523121591812 km/s) exclude 46% of target eclipsing-binary configurations.
No phase-0.5 data: secondary eclipses are unconstrained.
No odd/even depth measurement: twice-the-period binaries are only judged on shape.
Target scenarios assume the light curve is already corrected for neighbours' contaminating flux; eclipsing companions at other periods (x2P for bound/background stars) are not modelled.
